ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AE \perp BD$, $CD \perp BD$, $AB = BC$, $BE = CD$. What is the measure of $\angle ABC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because AE\perp BD$, $CD\perp BD$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEB=\angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\
In $Rt\triangle AEB$ and $Rt\triangle BDC$\\
$\because \left\{\begin{array}{l}AB=BC\\ BE=CD\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore Rt\triangle AEB\cong Rt\triangle BDC$,\\
$\therefore \angle A=\angle CBD$,\\
$\because \angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle A+\angle ABE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ABE+\angle CBD=\angle ABE+\angle A=90^\circ$.\\
Hence, the measure of $\angle ABC$ is $\boxed{90^\circ}$.

Set coordinates with B = (0,0) and BD as the positive x-axis. Let E = (u,0) and D = (v,0). Because AE and CD are perpendicular to BD and A,C are on opposite sides as shown, write A = (u,-h) and C = (v,k), with positive h,k. From the text BE = CD, so u = k. From AB = BC, get u^2 + h^2 = v^2 + k^2. Substituting k = u gives h^2 = v^2, hence h = v. Therefore vectors BA and BC can be represented as (u,-v) and (v,u). Their dot product is uv - vu = 0, so BA is perpendicular to BC. Hence angle ABC = 90°.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Given $\because AE\perp BD$, $CD\perp BD$,\\ $\therefore \angle AEB=\angle BDC=90^\circ$,\\ In $Rt\triangle AEB$ and $Rt\triangle BDC$,\\ $\because \left\{\begin{array}{l}AB=BC\\ BE=CD\end{array}\right.$,\\ $\therefore Rt\triangle AEB\cong Rt\triangle BDC$,\\ $\therefore \angle A=\angle CBD$,\\ $\because \angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle A+\angle ABE=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ABE+\angle CBD=\angle ABE+\angle A=90^\circ$.\\ Hence, the measure of $\angle ABC$ is $\boxed{90^\circ}$.

First describe the image: In the figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above and slightly to the right, and line segments AB and BC form angle ABC. Points E and D are located on line segment BD extending from B toward the interior, and BD divides ∠ABC into ∠ABE and ∠CBD. There are right-angle marks in the figure, corresponding to AE ⟂ BD and CD ⟂ BD, so ∠AEB and ∠BDC are both right angles.

Then reason: Because AE ⟂ BD and CD ⟂ BD, △AEB and △BDC are both right triangles. It is known that AB = BC, and BE = CD, among which AB and BC are respectively the hypotenuses of the two right triangles, and BE and CD are corresponding right sides. Therefore Rt△AEB ≅ Rt△BDC. From the equality of corresponding angles of congruent triangles, obtain ∠BAE = ∠CBD. In Rt△AEB, ∠BAE + ∠ABE = 90°. Also it can be seen from the figure that ∠ABC = ∠ABE + ∠CBD. Substituting ∠CBD = ∠BAE, get ∠ABC = ∠ABE + ∠BAE = 90°.
